title: Unique points of base-change fibres
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $k\to k\prime$ be a field extension, and let $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $\dim |C|\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put $C_{k\prime}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\prime$ and let $\pi:C_{k\prime}\to C$ be the projection [def-pc-base-change]. For every $c\in|C|$, there exists exactly one $z\in|C_{k\prime}|$ with $\pi(z)=c$.

proof.text: Apply geometry to conclude that every c is closed and its residue-field map is an isomorphism. Identify its residue field with k by residueFieldIsoBase.

Use Scheme.Pullback.carrierEquiv and its projection identities. Spec k and Spec k-prime each have one point, so triplets over a fixed c have only that choice of second point. The residue-field pushout is isomorphic to k-prime because the first map is an isomorphism; its spectrum has exactly one point. Transport existence and uniqueness back across carrierEquiv.
